title: Jaubert: credere Deo without charity is dead; credere in Deum living in the just alone
source_text: III. Hanc fidei distinctionem prolixe & accurate tradit Jaubertus Archiepiscopus Arelatensis, Tomo primo adversus Molinaei clypeum, cap. 40. in cujus initio observat fidem bifariam sumi: Primo pro actu vel habitu supernaturali mentis, per quem credimus verum quicquid in Scriptura continetur, & quicquid Deus revelavit, idque quia Deus dixit & revelavit; qui actus exprimitur in Scholis per credere Deo, & potest esse sine charitate, & bonis operibus; ac tum fides mortua vocatur, quoniam charitatis vita destituitur: Secundo vero aliam esse fidem quae dicitur viva, quia charitate animata est, atque per eam operatur: & fidei hujus actus exprimitur per credere in Deum, eaque in solo justo reperitur; ac per eam homo sperat & expectat promissionum divinarum complementum.
pass_a_gloss: This distinction of faith Jaubert, Archbishop of Arles, treats at length and carefully in the first Tomus against Molinaeus's shield, chapter 40, at whose beginning he observes that faith is taken in two ways: First for a supernatural act or habit of the mind by which we believe true whatever is contained in Scripture and whatever God has revealed, and that because God said and revealed it; which act is expressed in the Schools by believing God, and can be without charity and good works; and then faith is called dead, because it is destitute of the life of charity: Second, that there is another faith which is called living, because it is animated by charity and works through it; and the act of this faith is expressed by believing in God, and it is found in the just alone; and through it a person hopes and expects the fulfillment of the divine promises.
pass_b_english: Jaubert of Arles, against Molinaeus's Clypeum, unfolds the split at length.
Credere Deo is supernatural mind-assent to whatever God revealed because God said it — possible without charity, and then called dead for lack of charity's life.
Credere in Deum is living faith animated by charity, found only in the just, and through it the person hopes for the fulfillment of the promises.
